VBO:0201222.summary: Affectionate company and playful curiosity recur in firsthand accounts of the Shichon, a Shih Tzu–Bichon Frise cross also called a Zuchon. Keepers describe adults joining daily walks, learning tricks and searching for hidden objects or treats. Some programs breed successive generations of this cross, with individuals and lines varying in both appearance and temperament.
VBO:0201222.shortDescription: A Shih Tzu–Bichon Frise cross whose keepers describe affectionate company, daily adventures and an appetite for games.

sources.title: Tiny Teddys — named keeper and adult-owner accounts
sources.evidence: Actual signed Jyvanie and Thor account: fourth birthday, beach and forest trips, new tricks, treat puzzles, object searching, curious learning and sweet company. Actual Karen and Ken adult Oskar accounts: turns 13; separate preceding 12-year account records three daily walks, nightly floor play and accompanying owner at home office and RV trips. Bonnie and Bailey eight-year account records teaching a paw trick and close daily company. Original Mike and Corinne keeper account identifies multigenerational Shichon/Zuchon Shih Tzu–Bichon cross program, parent dogs sharing walks and naps; recognition is a future aim, not established fact. These actual observations support scoped recurring keeper tendencies, not universals.
